_: The SPEC §11.8.2 conformance fixtures: one scripted flow, one set of inputs, one
set of expected outputs, asserted by every binding. Authored once here and pinned
as literals by each suite — crates/misty-ffi/tests/native.rs (the exported UniFFI
and crates/misty-ffi/tests/web.rs (the wasm bundle in a headless browser).
The inputs are also served to foreign code at runtime by mock_fixtures(), so no
suite re-derives a device id or a key. The expected OUTPUTS are deliberately not
served that way: a suite that asked the core what to expect would be asserting the
core against itself. They are literals, and changing one means changing it in every
suite — which is exactly the review moment §11.8 wants.
Every secret here is an obvious dummy, as §8 requires of fixtures in a public repo.
notes: `code` is exact rather than a length check because the clock is pinned: FixedClock
at now_ms on the Rust side, and no runtime is allowed to read a wall clock (§11.7).
A binding that computed 6 digits of the wrong value would pass a length assertion.
`enroll` is represented by the mock core's pre-signed two-device roster rather than
a live §6.3 relay handshake: the joining half of enrollment needs core types
(Enrollment, SyncClient) that are quarantined behind the facade and have no FFI
projection. The live relay path is covered in Rust by
Assertions are on DTO values and on the stable error `code` string only, never on
`message` — so wording and localization can change without breaking the gate
